findings.title: Observing one project erases other projects’ polling state
findings.description: `RunnerTenant` shares one observer across projects, but each `observe()` retains only the current project’s entries. Visiting project B—even with no runs—deletes A’s poll timestamps, overdue markers, and cached faults. Consequently, A is polled every tick instead of respecting `run_poll_interval_seconds`, and least-recently-polled fairness breaks. Scope observer state and cleanup per project; add a multi-project regression test.

findings.title: Launch can start after the budget expires or shutdown is requested
findings.description: The budget check precedes journal creation and its synchronous database commit. If that operation consumes the remaining deadline, or a stop request arrives during it, `launch()` still starts the subprocess without another check. Pass the budget through to the launch boundary and explicitly handle a journaled command whose launch is deferred. Test deadline expiry and shutdown during `journal_issue()`.

findings.title: Unconfirmed launches falsely recover between failed polls
findings.description: A failed launch poll caches `RUN_OBSERVATION_FAILED` in `_faulted`, but this interval-skipping branch never replays it. The next tick reports `LAUNCHING` without that fault, allowing `ProjectTick._close_recovered()` to close the escalation despite no successful observation. Replay standing poll faults here, as `_confirmed()` does, and test consecutive ticks with fresh fault collections.

findings.title: Runtime validation was unavailable
findings.description: The local interpreter lacks `pydantic`; type checking also encountered unresolved dependencies. Tests and a clean strict-typecheck result could not be verified.
